parsed.main_gap: Pigeonhole in Section 5 miscounts: nonempty proper subsets give 2^{n+1}-3 gaps summing to <1, which only yields a gap <1/(2^{n+1}-3), not ≤ d; the claim is false as stated (n=1, lengths 0.9, 0.1). Fix: include ∅ and the full set.

errors.description: The deduction of (11)/(12) is invalid: 2^{n+1}-3 gaps summing to less than 1 do not give a gap ≤ 1/(2^{n+1}-1). With only nonempty proper subsets the claim fails (n=1, a=(0.9,0.1): the only gap is 0.8 > 1/3). The correct argument uses all 2^{n+1} subsets including ∅ and the full set (2^{n+1}-1 gaps summing to exactly 1); the resulting A or B may then be empty, which the write-up's next case already handles.
errors.quote:
They lie in $(0,1)$, so their $2^{n+1}-3$ consecutive gaps sum to less than $1$. When put in nondecreasing order, two consecutive subset sums therefore differ by at most
\[
\frac1{2^{n+1}-1}=d. \tag{11}
\]

parsed.notes: Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) correct. Claiming-stage reduction to alternating discrepancy, pairing characterization, tree-component/powers-of-two lower bound, and common-refinement cut count are all verified correct. Only defect is the subset-sum pigeonhole count, a one-line repair whose consequences the case analysis already covers.
